functional_sequences.mechanism: Colonic epithelial transport changes the fluid composition of luminal contents; absorption and secretion have different directions and depend on physiological conditions.

steps.narration: Identify the flat luminal surface and crypt openings. This crop contains no villi.
Colonocytes support net sodium and chloride uptake. Water movement accompanies solute transport; net movement changes with luminal composition and osmolality.
The epithelium also secretes potassium and bicarbonate. Chloride/bicarbonate exchange illustrates opposite directions; neither direction is universal under all conditions.
Relate epithelial exchange to stromal and vascular support. The supplied arterial feeders and venules do not constitute a connected exchange capillary bed.

schematic_limitations: No ion channels, pumps, tight-junction pathways, concentrations, osmotic gradients or exchange capillary bed are represented.
No flow-rate, absorption fraction or transit-time calculation; manual view changes are not measured fluid transport.
Do not teach the supplied generic venular sugars/amino-acids text as the main colonic function.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Goblet-cell mucin secretion helps separate luminal microbes from epithelium; a structured mucus barrier has functions beyond lubrication.

steps.narration: Find goblet cells in the crypt epithelial complement and on the surface; their mucin secretion contributes to mucus.
Explain the attached dense inner mucus barrier above the epithelial surface. Mouse Muc2 experiments show bacterial exclusion here.
Explain the expanded outer mucus domain that accommodates microbes. Both mucus domains and bacteria are narrated, not rendered in this model.

schematic_limitations: There is no mucus mesh, microbial population, secretion morph or permeability solver; no layer visibility toggle may be described as mucus secretion.
The directly opened two-layer experiment is in mice; its thickness is not assigned to this human teaching crop.
Goblet counts are sampled teaching counts, not cell density or measured secretory capacity.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Crypt-base progenitors maintain epithelial lineages; renewal is explained from basal source to epithelial destination.

steps.narration: Locate the sampled crypt-base stem cells. Adult mouse Lgr5 lineage tracing supports their ability to generate epithelial lineages.
Trace the conceptual connection from basal progenitors to absorptive and secretory epithelial lineages; transit-amplifying cells are not separate parts.
Relate continued cell production to maintenance of the luminal lining. An upward renewal path is a teaching inference; the meshes remain stationary.

schematic_limitations: Six basal cells per crypt are authored samples, not a biological census.
No division, differentiation, migration or extrusion trajectories are simulated.
No fixed human turnover interval or deterministic APC-to-cancer progression is claimed.

functional_sequences.mechanism: Enteric circuits coordinate muscle activity and epithelial transport; the two plexuses indicate major anatomical control regions, not exclusive functional ownership.

steps.narration: Locate the myenteric plexus between the external muscle layers. Neural signals regulate gut muscle contraction and relaxation.
Explain narrowing by circular muscle and shortening by longitudinal muscle. Coordinated activation contributes to mixing and propulsion; the local sheet is not a whole-colon contraction wave.
Locate the submucosal plexus near mucosa. Human studies show projections to mucosa, submucosa and circular muscle; secretion and motility control overlap.
Return to epithelial targets to connect neural regulation with fluid handling. The native plexus meshes do not identify individual synapses or transmitter classes.

schematic_limitations: No connected neuron-to-effector circuit, synapses, interstitial cells of Cajal, electrical slow waves or extrinsic autonomic pathways are modeled.
No muscle deformation or luminal-content displacement is supplied; advancing stages is manual explanation.
Do not equate one taenia marker with all three bands or infer a complete haustral contraction.

functional_sequences.mechanism: An organized solitary follicle and the surrounding diffuse mucosal immune compartment have related but distinct teaching roles.

steps.narration: Locate the solitary follicle in this crop’s lamina propria. Human colonic follicles can extend into submucosa; this supplied follicle is wholly mucosal.
Identify the follicular mantle around the germinal-centre compartment. A germinal centre represents a secondary follicle; not every normal human follicle contains one.
Explain organized follicles as sites of local immune induction and lamina propria as a diffuse effector compartment. Antigen sampling and cell traffic are conceptual here.

schematic_limitations: No follicle-associated epithelium, M cells, antigen-presenting cells, T cells, plasma cells, lymphatics or antibody transport machinery are separate selectable parts.
The visible germinal centre is a structural teaching example, not an assertion that every follicle is active or that all IgA switching occurs inside germinal centres.
This crop cannot demonstrate antigen transit, affinity selection, antibody secretion or an infection response.

sources.title: Billich and Levitan 1969: intact human colon water/electrolyte perfusion
sources.scope: Primary human study; net transport depends on luminal composition and osmolality. No fixed model rate.

sources.title: Hawker et al. 1978: transport of Na, Cl and K in human colon
sources.scope: Primary isolated human mucosa; active sodium/chloride absorption and potassium secretion; no molecular pump geometry inferred.

sources.title: Davis et al. 1983: chloride/bicarbonate exchange in human colon
sources.scope: Primary human perfusion; chloride absorption with bicarbonate secretion; bicarbonate can also be absorbed in other conditions.

sources.title: Johansson et al. 2008: Muc2-dependent colonic mucus layers
sources.scope: Primary mouse experiment: attached inner bacteria-excluding layer and expanded colonized outer layer. Species qualification retained; not a human thickness target.

sources.title: Barker et al. 2007: Lgr5 crypt-base stem cells
sources.scope: Opened abstract and publisher figure captions; adult mouse lineage tracing supports crypt-base cells generating epithelial lineages. Not proof of a universal human turnover interval.

sources.title: Porter et al. 1999: human colonic submucosal neuronal projections
sources.scope: Primary human preparation; submucosal projections reach mucosa, submucosa and circular muscle; prevents an absolute motility-versus-secretion split.

sources.title: NIDDK: Your Digestive System and How It Works
sources.scope: Federal authoritative teaching source: enteric neural signals regulate muscle contraction/relaxation; peristalsis moves and mixes contents.

sources.title: Gebbers et al. 1992: human large-bowel lymphoid follicle structure and function
sources.scope: Primary human histology: follicle-associated epithelium, B-cell compartment, variable germinal-centre presence, inductive follicle versus effector lamina propria.
